expected_level_description: You can: - set information governance policy and strategy - advise the board on information risk and compliance - represent the organisation with regulators and partners

You can: - set the organisation's data protection impact assessment process and standards - give the final advice on the highest-risk processing, such as large-scale data sharing or AI - consult regulators where the law requires it

You can: - set the incident management process for information governance - lead the response to major breaches, including with regulators and the media - report incident trends and risks to the board
You can: - own the organisation's information governance assurance framework - report assurance and compliance to the board and its committees - set improvement priorities based on risk

You can: - advise on complex confidentiality questions, such as sharing without consent in the public interest - review information sharing agreements with partner organisations - apply consent and patient objection rules to data flows
You can: - run the governance cycle for boards and committees - review policies and advise on compliance

You can: - oversee compliance with data ethics standards and legislation across the organisation - develop, manage and continuously improve an ethical framework within your area - develop a data ethics culture, influencing others to act on it - ensure data ethics is applied appropriately when formulating, implementing and evaluating organisational policies and programmes

You can: - work with the team to develop and maintain an understanding of stakeholders - work with the team to develop and implement stakeholder communications strategies - identify and resolve issues, influence stakeholders and manage relationships effectively - build long-term strategic relationships and communicate clearly and regularly with stakeholders
